entry: Ran src/standalone/session-state-patch.mjs (diffSessionState/applySessionStatePatch), session-service.mjs createSessionService().handleCall with scripted sessionExists / readStoredSession / subscribeExternalSessionStates / onFrame, channel-transport.mjs createChannelTransport over real HTTP on 127.0.0.1 (behind a TCP tap), the real session transport + session-client attachSession with the stub runtime of scripts/session-transport/_shared.mjs, and, for 192/446/493, the real session client against a scripted HTTP daemon (the test's own stand-in, a recorder-side http.createServer) behind the tap. Every HTTP exchange (status line, headers in order, body; an event stream as its frames) is recorded. Did not run the identity case 19.
exclusions: case 19 is listed in notRecorded with its reason

wire taps record the HTTP exchanges in request order: `Host` header port value -> <port> and the response `Date` header value -> <date>, at those header paths; and this machine's roots (the checkout process.cwd() -> <CWD>, the OS temp dir -> <TMP>, the user home -> <HOME>, in every spelling found: as written, forward slashes, JSON-escaped, URL-encoded, each also lower-cased; text after the root, separators included, is kept) in every request/response startLine, header value, body and event-stream frame (lib/tmp-mark.mjs). The Content-Length is the one Node sent: a message that had a root replaced carries `rewrites` {label: {originalLength, count}} (a label for a spelling other than as written reads "<CWD> (JSON-escaped)"), so length(recorded body) + sum(count * (originalLength - label length)) = Content-Length. No other value is normalised
case 303: written through the transport's `_writeRemoteStateToForTest` hook (the same function the pointer uses) because the production writer needs a displaced client

cases 446 and 493 move virtual clocks: 446 ticks the mocked global setTimeout (only setTimeout is faked; sockets keep their own timers), 493 moves Date.now() by recorded steps while the client's own 5-20 ms timers run in real time and the scripted daemon holds every reconnect until released
crypto.randomUUID returns 00000000-0000-4000-8000-<12-digit counter> in call order (client tokens, registration ids, server tokens, daemon session ids, call ids all come from it)
crypto.randomBytes(n) (without a callback) returns the next n values of a running byte counter modulo 256
Date.now() is 1700000000000 and performance.now() is 0 for the whole run (revisions are Date.now()*1000, queuedMs is 0) unless a case moves the virtual clock by a recorded step
process.pid is 4242 (process.kill(pid, 0) of it answers alive, as it is this process) and process.ppid is 4241; the recorded cwd is the constant "C:\\recorded\\cwd"

GLOBALS PATCHED by installDeterminism(): crypto.randomUUID, crypto.randomBytes (no-callback form), Date.now, performance.now, process.pid, process.ppid, process.kill (signal 0 of the fixed pid only). The child-process preloads (lib/determinism-preload.mjs, determinism-preload-other-process.mjs) patch crypto.randomUUID, crypto.randomBytes, Date.now and process.pid only (pid 4242, the second process 4243); they leave process.kill, performance.now and process.ppid alone

BRANCH process.pid liveness (isPidAlive / process.kill(pid, 0): src/runtime/shared/pid-liveness.mjs, ~54 files: daemon discovery in session-client, writer and process locks): the fixed pid is answered alive by the process.kill hook in the recording process; a child process preloaded with the fixed pid has no such hook, so it would judge the parent's pid dead and could steal a lock the parent held: no recorded flow has a lock held across processes (restart-prefix phases run one after the other, the lifecycle parent holds nothing while its child runs)

BRANCH process.pid equality (own-lock re-entrancy, ~33 sites such as memory-process-lock, scheduler): a recorded flow with two processes gives them different pids (4242, 4243) so they are different owners, as in production

BRANCH id collision: session ids are sess_<pid>_<n>_<Date.now()>_<randomBytes(16)>; with a fixed pid, a fixed or stepped clock and a counter for the bytes, uniqueness rests on the store's own sequence number n (nextId) and on the counters not being reset between live sessions: determinism.reset() is called only where the previous session is finished (lifecycle fresh()), and a collision would fail the save, not pass unnoticed

BRANCH ordering by time (~23 sort sites on updatedAt/createdAt): with a fixed clock timestamps tie, so a listing sorted by time falls back to insertion order; no recorded case reads a time-ordered listing of several sessions (directory listings are recorded in the OS order)

BRANCH deadlines on Date.now / performance.now (~74 performance.now sites, Date.now deadline loops such as settleTurnJournalWrites and lock timeouts): with the clock fixed they never expire inside the code under test; every wait of a recorder carries its own real-timer deadline instead, and the cases that need elapsed time move the virtual clock by a recorded step

case 446, compared whole from the recorded steps (silent_connection.rs): each step's event-stream count and disconnects; not compared: the step's prose, Node's `ok` (its scripted daemon answered `{}` and its client returns undefined; the core's answer is the `{}` result), the disconnect's reason text ("sse aborted") and the wire's HTTP exchanges

case 192, compared from the recorded steps (silent_connection.rs a_connection_the_server_ends_is_reconnected_and_a_call_meanwhile_is_answered): the call's answer, the fatals and the reconnect's attempt (Node counts from 1, the core from 0: the core's attempt is shown plus one); not compared: Node's `registrations` (its client registers once and reopens only the event stream; the core's connection is one socket, so a reconnect is a new initialize), the reconnect's reason text and downtimeMs, and the wire's HTTP exchanges

patch.applied: to a temporary copy of the tree's src for the second recording of case 327 only; every other case runs the unpatched tree
patch.fixes: src/standalone/channel-transport/remote-state.mjs: String(null) published Remote as enabled for the session "null" (case 327, first state)

product.tree: product tree loaded by the recorder

replay: Replayed over the transport harness of native/core/crates/mixdog-app-server/src/tests/wire.rs: the server behind its real WebSocket listener on a loopback port, real client connections driven as the daemon drives them, over a real session thread. Every frame each client received is compared whole and in order (session_transport.rs whole); the only normalization is wire::normalized: ids the core generates become <id:N> in order of first appearance and clock readings (*At fields, clientHostPid) become <clock>/<pid>. The recorded HTTP exchanges (wire: start lines, headers, Content-Length) are Node's HTTP/SSE framing of each call; the core's client transport is one WebSocket carrying each JSON-RPC message as one text frame (mixdog-app-server-transport websocket.rs), so the frame bodies are compared and the HTTP framing has no counterpart. Cases: 67 an_unknown_thread_is_refused_and_nothing_is_created, 94 an_unsubscribed_client_receives_nothing_more, 365 every_attached_client_folds_the_same_items (the desktop's prompt, sent while the terminal's runs, waits in the thread's queue and runs next: the core runs one turn at a time), 303 remote_state_churn_with_no_reader_leaves_only_the_latest (10000 hostState.remoteSession publications with no client, then a client attaching receives one snapshot holding the latest). 327 (--with-the-fix) is replayed by mixdog-services channels/tests_runtime.rs the_bridge_binding_publishes_the_pinned_session_as_node_does: every hostState.remoteSession publication whole, Node's frames applied as the desktop applies them (session-host-publication.ts:290); Node's second frame is the client registration adding its cwd, which has no core counterpart (no channel transport client registers). 428 is replayed by mixdog-app-server-daemon late_lifecycle.rs the_last_client_connection_closing_stops_the_core_as_nodes_clients_empty through the server's connection entry (client_opened/client_closed); Node's connectionCount also counts its in-daemon transport connection (lifecycle:false), and the core's in-daemon callers use CallContext::internal, never a connection, so the core's count is Node's minus that one. 48 is replayed by session_transport.rs a_tool_result_on_a_long_transcript_sends_only_the_changed_item (1999 stored rows, a tool call updated by its result: the client receives the changed item, the context, the turn's end and the idle runtime as events, Node's patch being `busy: false` and the rows from 1999). 275 is replayed by a_client_attaching_after_a_large_state_receives_it_once (a client that attaches after the session grew to a 160 KiB prompt receives its state once as the snapshot). 446 is replayed by mixdog-app-server-client tests/it/silent_connection.rs a_silent_connection_is_kept_until_its_socket_closes (the core's client keeps a connection the server leaves silent for the recorded 600000 ms, answers a call on it, and reports the socket closing). Also replayed by mixdog-app-server-client silent_connection.rs: 192 (the server ends the connection, a call made meanwhile is answered after the reconnect, no fatal, the reconnect reported as attempt 1; exclusions in `exclusions`). Not replayed: 493 (Node's client ends a silent event stream after its liveness timeout, 20 ms in the recording, and gives up when reconnects keep failing for 60 ms of wall time; the core's client has neither: it keeps a silent connection, which 446's replay shows, and its reconnect ladder retries until the client is closed); 327 base commit (records the String(null) defect the patch fixes).
